title: Signature Drift Sentry and Compatibility Orchestrator for Function-style Outputs
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight, production-ready service that detects semantic and structural drift in function-style outputs (function calls / structured tool invocations) during staged rollouts and orchestrates automated mitigations (soft-shim, traffic quarantine, and auto-unwind).

Context: We've seen flaky failures in a small set of canaries when rolling model variants that change how function arguments are serialized (types, optional fields, renamed keys) leading to downstream executor errors. Existing diffs and schema checks are noisy for benign reorderings and non-impacting formatting changes. We need a risk-aware sentinel that: (1) correlates structural diffs with downstream tool success, (2) applies minimal runtime shims where possible, and (3) triggers safe rollback policies when caller compatibility drops below SLOs.

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: detect per-invocation compatibility regressions across canary slices, produce scalar scores for routing policies, and integrate auto-unwind. Implement conservative shims (field aliasing, type coercion, safe defaults). Provide dashboards and alerts.
- Non-goal: do not ship an ML-based repair model in this phase (we'll rely on deterministic adapters and heuristics).

Design summary:
1) Fingerprinting: build compact invocation fingerprints capturing ordered argument names, presence flags, argument types (string/number/object/array/null), and normalized enum values. Fingerprints are small tokens and are stored in a time-windowed histogram per model variant + per-route.
2) Diff scoring: compute three signals per fingerprint delta: structural distance (Jaccard of keys + positional mismatches), type-mismatch rate, and downstream failure correlation (post-call error rate). Combine into a single Compatibility Divergence Score (CDS) in [0,1].
3) Shim layer: when CDS is in the caution band (0.2-0.5) for a slice, attempt a best-effort shim: alias key rename mappings, coerce strings->numbers when safe, inject explicit nulls for missing optional fields, and drop obviously extraneous keys. Shims are applied only to canary traffic and recorded for auditing.
4) Shadow and probe strategy: mirror 100% of incoming production calls into a shadow sink for the candidate variant. For traffic routed to the candidate, send a sampled secondary invocation to the baseline (golden) variant to compute invocation parity metrics.
5) Abort and auto-unwind: define hard thresholds (CDS >= 0.6 sustained over 5m with downstream failure increase > 2x baseline) to trigger an automated rollback. Include hysteresis windows and allow safety-net manual override.

Telemetry & observability:
- Per-route metrics: invocation_count, fingerprint_uniqueness, CDS_p50/p90, shim_applied_rate, downstream_success_rate, mean_time_to_repair.
- Dashboards: "Signature Drift Overview", "Shim Effectiveness", and per-customer slice drilldowns.
- Alerts: CDS_critical (>=0.6), AnchorRegression (candidate downstream_failure_rate > baseline * 2), and ShimFailureRate (>10%).

Operational playbook (high level):
- Stage 1 (shadow-only): enable shadowing for new variant and collect fingerprints for 24h or 100k invocations. Compute baseline histograms.
- Stage 2 (canary ramp): 1% -> 5% -> 20% ramp with sampled gold baseline comparisons and enable shims in the caution band.
- Stage 3 (widen): if CDS_p90 < 0.2 and shim_applied_rate < 2%, continue ramp. If CDS shows oscillation, keep canary at a fixed slice and increase sampling.
- Auto-unwind: when thresholds breach, automatically revert traffic within 30s and open an incident with attached fingerprint diff and examples.

Integration points and artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Signature+Drift+Sentry+Spec
- Design mockups (shim config UI): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/shim-ui-prototypes
- Initial PR (implementation skeleton): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1256

Trade-offs & rationale:
- We accept a small fraction of false positives by design because conservative automatic rollback reduces customer-visible outages.
- The shim layer is intentionally limited to deterministic transforms to avoid divergent behavior between candidate and baseline.
- We store only aggregated histograms for privacy and cost; raw payloads are persisted separately behind customer consent and TAP for replay.

Next steps:
- Spike a prototype scorer + shim executor in the runtime canary environment (Marco).
- Add dashboard tiles and alerts (SRE + Observability).
- Run two internal canaries (payments route and search-route) and evaluate shim effectiveness over 2 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype scorer computes CDS and reports p50/p90 for three test routes
Shim executor can apply aliasing + safe coercions with telemetry hooks and audit logs
Shadow histogram collection is enabled and stored for 30 days in observability cluster
Automated rollback is triggered when CDS >= 0.6 with downstream failure > 2x baseline (test harness validates)
Dashboards and PagerDuty runbook exist and are linked from the ticket

comments: 2026-02-12 - Priya Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Agreed to focus first on function-style outputs (name+args) and not generic JSON shape diffing. Action: Marco to spike fingerprinter.

2026-02-18 - Marco Chen: Spike done. Fingerprinter prototype pushed to PR #1256. Found that arrays of objects with non-deterministic ordering caused many false positives; introducing key sorting + stable hashing reduced noise by ~72% on sample set.
2026-02-22 - Aisha Raman (SRE): Observability checklist reviewed. We must include per-tenant sampling limits to avoid cost blowup. I've added draft alert thresholds; will iterate after canary data.

2026-02-28 - Marco Chen: Early shim test on search-route canary: aliasing 'user_id' <-> 'uid' avoided 18% of downstream failures. Coercion rules caused 1% spurious conversions; disabled coercion for enums pending safer logic.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Liam O'Neill): Shim UI wires look good. Request: surface example transformations and allow opt-out per-tenant. UX/PM approved on principle.
2026-03-05 - Priya Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include audit logs and runbook. Next milestone: validate auto-unwind behavior in staging with synthetic breaches.
parent_issue_notes: This ticket extends the staged-deploy fingerprinting work and focuses specifically on automated mitigation and rollback orchestration.
